summary: Pair of 1889 wooden range lights at Kinlock, Prince Edward Island, marking the approach to Charlottetown Harbour; keepers' stints from 1890 and the lights automated after 1958.

structures.note: Raised by about 2.4 m around 1948; moved back from the bank in 1902 and 1936. The Coast Guard list and LighthouseFriends give 17.3 m; Rowlett gives 14 m (47 ft).
Stands 650 m north of the front range light on a hill. The Coast Guard list and LighthouseFriends give 14 m; Rowlett gives 12 m (37 ft).

access.note: Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. Site and tower closed (Rowlett). The access lane is private and visitors are not openly welcome (LighthouseFriends). Set in a residential area (Parks Canada).

events.note: Two pairs of range lights established to guide vessels into Charlottetown Harbour
Range lights changed from fixed red to fixed white
Front tower moved back from the bank
Vapour installations (25 mm) listed for the front and back lights
Edwin Stewart appointed keeper of both range lights at $320 a year
Lights automated by 1958 at the latest: Stewart retired that year and then served as caretaker of the automated lights (LighthouseFriends). The date of automation is not given.
Parks Canada register gives Stewart's service as ending in 1961 (disputed; LighthouseFriends says 1958)

notes_for_editor: 1) Colour: the Coast Guard list gives F W (cite 6); Rowlett and LighthouseFriends say yellow (cites 7, 2); the record's Wikidata source says F Y. Not resolved; the story says so. 2) Stewart's end date: 1958 (LighthouseFriends, cite 2) against 1961 (Parks Canada register, cite 1). Not resolved; the story says so. The register dates put his service past 1960, so he is named only as the sources name him, as keeper, with the salary figures LighthouseFriends prints. 3) Heights: the Coast Guard list (cite 6) and LighthouseFriends (cites 2, 3) give the front tower 17.3 m and the rear 14.0 m; Rowlett (cite 7) gives the front 14 m (47 ft) and the rear 12 m (37 ft). The story states the disagreement. 4) Keepers: front-light stints come from LighthouseFriends (cite 3); rear-light stints from LighthouseFriends (cite 2) and the register (cite 1), which covers the rear light only. The Department's 1902 and 1910 keeper tables were not used for names because the OCR columns cannot be matched reliably. Beaton's 1907 entry (cite 8) was matched by row position and checked on the page image (scan 154, printed p. 147): the row reads Beaton, Angus S | Hazard Point Range, Black Light | Nov. 21, 1902. McRae's appointment of 6 April 1900 (1910 table) is noted, not used. 5) The 1889 establishment rests on the register and LighthouseFriends; the Department's pre-1900 reports are not in the local corpus. 6) No wrecks, storms or rescues were found for these lights in the sources read; the storms chapter is omitted. 7) Tower colours: LighthouseFriends describes both towers as red-faced with black stripes (cite 2); the Coast Guard list gives white pyramid towers with red tops (cite 6); Rowlett gives red lanterns and front faces with black stripes (cite 7). Colour of the towers is not in the story. 8) The 1958 automation date is not in any source; the event is recorded as 'by 1958' only. 9) Not used: Wikipedia; the PEI Lighthouse Society page was not read.
